The register says applicant: "Emerson Process Management Micro Motion Inc." and the document says "Micro Motion, Inc."

The register name "Emerson Process Management Micro Motion Inc." is the full legal corporate name — Micro Motion is a subsidiary of Emerson Process Management, and the full legal entity name on certificates is often "Micro Motion, Inc." while corporate registry lists "Emerson Process Management Micro Motion Inc." Actually, Micro Motion, Inc. is the manufacturer; Emerson Process Management is the parent. The applicant/manufacturer on the certificate reads "Micro Motion, Inc." — the register's value appears to be a concatenation of the parent brand (Emerson Process Management) and the operating company (Micro Motion Inc.). This is a known legal name drift: the same legal entity, with the register using the fuller corporate style. This is not two different companies. It's the same entity — legal-suffix/corporate-style drift, arguably.

Is it "same-entity"? Emerson Process Management is the parent; Micro Motion is a division/brand of Emerson Process Management. In OIML certificates for Micro Motion products, the applicant is often listed as "Emerson Process Management GmbH & Co. OHG" or "Micro Motion, Inc." Micro Motion, Inc. is the manufacturer (Boulder, Colorado). The register's "Emerson Process Management Micro Motion Inc." is likely a fused/concatenated name from combining parent + subsidiary. Same entity in practice — the manufacturer is Micro Motion, Inc., a division of Emerson Process Management. The certificate is the legal instrument, so best_value should be the document's value: "Micro Motion, Inc."

Verdict: same-entity. best_value: "Micro Motion, Inc." (document's, since certificate is legal instrument; rule says for same-entity, use register's canonical form — but that rule is specifically for number/year formats. For same-entity names, what's best_value? The rules: spelling drift etc = same-entity, presumably best_value from document since certificate is the legal instrument (stated for different-entity). Hmm. The rules explicitly state best_value only for different-entity (document's) and document-noise (register's) and same-entity numbers (register's canonical). For same-entity names, the sensible choice is the document's value because the certificate is the legal instrument and its exact legal name matters. But one could argue the register's fuller name is more canonical.

I'd say same-entity, best_value = "Micro Motion, Inc." with why: the register's value concatenates the parent corporate brand (Emerson Process Management) with the subsidiary's legal name; the certificate's "Micro Motion, Inc." is the legal instrument's designation for the same manufacturer.
